HMGT 570.description: Strategic Management. Provides skill development and application in the integrative  discipline of strategic management including assessment, strategy  formulation implementation and control.  Open to MHM students only.

HMGT 575.description: Managing and Improving Health. Methods for monitoring and improving the health of populations.   Topics include outcomes management, risk-adjustment, development  and implementation of practice guidelines.  Open to MHM students  only.

HMGT 600.description: Managing Risk. Overview of reimbursement models in clinical and institutional settings; legal, financial and clinical assumption of risk pursuant to new and evolving federal and state statutory and regulatory provisions. Open only to EMHA students.

HMGT 603.description: Developing & Monitoring of Quality & Patient Safety Outcomes. Overview of contemporary methods used to develop and monitor patient quality and safety outcomes; develop skill in data collection and analysis of clinical care outcomes; focus on operationalizing outcomes that matter to payers, organizations, and clinicians. Open only to EMHA students.

HP 200.description: Introduction to Health Promotion and Disease     Prevention                                      . Introduction to strategies for promoting health and wellness. Includes self monitoring of health risk behavior, goal setting, and behavior changes.

HP 230.description: Nutrition and Health. Nutrition as it relates to health promotion across the lifespan  and disease prevention.  Discussion of nutrients, factors  affecting food choices, food safety and global nutrition issues.

HP 270.description: Introduction to Global Health. Introduction to concepts of global health and disease control.  Issues of globalization, global governance, emerging diseases,  infectious disease treatment, and outbreak challenges.

HP 290.description: Introduction to Research Apprenticeship. Individual research apprenticeship in health related fields under  supervision of a departmental faculty member.  Graded CR/NC.   Departmental approval.

HP 300.description: Principles of Human Behavior. Overview and analysis of human behavior and the influences of behavior on health and disease.

HP 320.description: Biological and Behavioral Basis of Disease. Examination of the major systems of the human body; disease  processes and behavioral risk factors.

HP 340.description: Health Behavior Statistical Methods. Intermediate statistics for health behavior studies; topics include descriptive statistics, hypothesis testing, correlation and regression, and use of computer software in data analysis.

HP 350.description: Health Behavior Research Methods. Introduction to the design, conduct and evaluation of health  behavior research studies; quantitative and qualitative approaches  to research and analysis. Recommended preparation: HP 340L

HP 365.description: Culture, Lifestyle, and Health. Comparison of national and international differences in health status as influenced by cultural practices and lifestyles within geographic, economic, and political environments.

HP 370.description: Introduction to Epidemiology: Methods and Applications. Examines the primary goals and methods of epidemiology, the study of factors that influence health and disease in individuals and populations.

HP 408.description: Environmental Health in the Community. Survey of occupational and environmental health. Introduction to  epidemiology, exposure assessment, toxicology, policy development,  risk assessment, and effects of urban development on health.

HP 420.description: Gender and Minority Health Issues. Examines the nature and roots of health disparities among women,men, and different ethnic and age groups; methods for reducing such disparities; strategies for prevention services.

HP 421.description: Violence as a Public Health Issue. Patterns and prevalence of violence; psychosoical, environmental,  and biological influences on violent behavior; youth gangs; drugs  and violence; family violence; and prevention and intervention  strategies.

HP 430.description: Obesity and Health. Examination of causes and consequences of obesity, with emphasis  on health risks of type II diabetes and cardiovascular disease.   Recommended preparation: HP 230.

HP 442.description: Chronic Disease Epidemiology. Overview of causative factors and demographic distributions of the  major chronic diseases in the western world; edpidemiologic  concepts and research designs.  Recommended preparation: HP 320

HP 450.description: Traditional Eastern Medicine and Modern Health. Overview of traditional Eastern approaches toward health and  disease; relevance to modern health issues, emphasizing a  comparison between traditional Chinese and modern Western medicine. Recommended Preparation:  Fundamentals of Medicine

HP 460.description: Adolescent Health. Survey of the development of healthy and the prevention of health-risk behaviors during adolescence. Prevention and promotion techniques will be explored emphasizing cultural differences.

HP 490.description: Directed Research. Individual research and readings. Not available for graduate credit. Open to HP majors only. Recommended preparation: HP 350L

HCDA 500.description: U.S. Health System: Healthcare Access and Delivery. Introduction to U.S. health system with comprehensive overview of insurance coverage and benefits, reimbursement, access to healthcare and biopharmaceuticals, and the delivery of healthcare services.

HCDA 502.description: Comparative International Healthcare Systems. Comparative analysis of healthcare coverage and financing policies across countries. Examine its relationship to drug coverage, access, reimbursement, pricing policies and impact on biopharmaceutical market.

HCDA 512.description: Applied Economic Analysis of U.S. Health Policies. Evaluate healthcare policies' costs and benefits for diverse stakeholders using case studies and quantitative methods. Equip yourself to advocate for policy changes with data-driven insights.

HCDA 520.description: Health Economic and Outcomes Methodology. Comprehensive review of the strategies used in drug value assessment with a focus on health economics and outcomes research and application to healthcare decision making.

HCDA 572.description: Introduction to Healthcare Data Analytics. Learn methods for working with large health data sets, including developing an analytic plan and selecting an appropriate data source, as well as practical skills needed to manage and use large health data sets to accomplish an analytic goal.

HCDA 580.description: Seminars in Healthcare Decision Analysis. Weekly seminar and literature series, review and discuss policy, biopharmaceuticals, insurance, global healthcare access issues. Student lead discussions, expert guest speakers, group projects, critical thinking.

HCDA 589.description: Healthcare Consulting Enterprise Team Project. Work as a consultant to conduct market research and apply decision analysis methods to design strategies for healthcare products and services or company pipelines.

HCDA 596.description: Internship for Curricular Practical Training. Part-time or full-time, practical work experience in the student's  field of study. The internship must be located at an off-campus  facility. Students are individually supervised by faculty. May not  be taken until the student has completed at least one full  academic year of enrollment in the graduate program with a  cumulative 3.0 GPA.

HEBR 120.description: Hebrew I.  Focuses on the acquisition of proficiency and communicative skills in speaking, reading, writing, and comprehension as well as cultural literacy.

HEBR 121.description: Hebrew for Business, Technology and Media. Effective communication in Hebrew, exploration of Israel's economy in the context of globalization, improving language skills for use in the global job market.

HEBR 220.description: Hebrew III.  Continuation of Hebrew II; stress on grammar, composition, and conversation. Prerequisite: HEBR 150.

EDHP 503.description: Curriculum, Teaching, and Learning in Higher, Adult, and Professional Education. Curriculum, teaching, and learning strategies for general, vocational, and professional education; planning for lifelong learning; theories, policies, and practices for higher, adult and professional education.

EDHP 587.description: Practicum in Higher, Adult and Professional Education. Structured participation in supervised teaching or administrative activities. Assignments matched with student's goals, training, experience.

EDHP 593A.description: Master's Seminar. An examination and analysis of research and literature in the  student's area of focus.  Required for all master's candidates who  do not enroll in the Master's Thesis (594abz).  Graded CR/NC.

EDHP 594A.description: Master's Thesis. Required for all master's candidates who do not enroll in the  Master's Seminar (593ab).  Credit on acceptance of thesis.  Graded  IP/CR/NC.

EDHP 594Z.description: Master's Thesis. Required for all master's candidates who do not enroll in the  Master's Seminar (593ab).  Credit on acceptance of thesis.  Graded  IP/CR/NC.

EDHP 679.description: Legal Issues in the Administration of Higher Education. Analysis of legal issues related to the administration of higher education; emphasis on relations with students, faculty, staff, alumni, and campus communities.

EDHP 687.description: Student Development in Higher Education.  Theories of college student development and application of developmental models to program design, interventions, outreach, and research programs.

HIST 103.description: The Emergence of Modern Europe. Political, intellectual, and cultural developments in Europe, 13001815. Renaissance and Reformation; absolute monarchy, scientific changes, and Enlightenment; French Revolution and Napoleon.

HIST 105.description: The Korean Past. A topical and chronological study of the major political, social, and intellectual forces that have shaped the history of Korea.

HIST 110.description: History of Early Africa. Surveys the major dynamics of economic and political change in Sub-Saharan Africa before the imposition of European colonial rule in the late nineteenth century.

HIST 201.description: Approaches to History. Methods and theories of historical interpretation of evidence; uses of archives; modes of presenting the past to the public. Required of all History majors. Duplicates credit in former HIST-300.

HIST 210.description: How to Be An American: Global Histories of U.S. Citizenship. History of United States citizenship from its origins to the present day, with particular attention to relationship between law and culture.

HIST 211.description: Race in America. Examines the origins of the idea of race and how this idea influenced the development of the United States from the colonial period to the present day.

HIST 240.description: History of California. A thematic approach to California history from precontact to present; focus on peoples, environment, economic, social, and cultural development, politics, and rise to global influence.

HIST 266.description: Business and East Asian Culture, 1800-Present. Business history of East Asia (China, Japan, Korea, Taiwan, and Hong Kong) as related to culture, politics, and society.

HIST 278.description: Ottomans and Empire: Anatolia, the Middle East,  and the Mediterranean World. Overview of the history of the Ottomans and their imperial subjects.

HIST 331.description: The British Empire: 1588-1834. Emergence of the British Empire, emphasizing colonies in the  Americas; the development of imperial economy, imperial wars,  slavery and abolitionism.

HIST 336.description: History of Japan, 1550-1945.  Development of Japan as a modern world power; tradition and change in Japanese life; impact of Western culture, politics, and diplomacy from 1550 to 1945.

HIST 354.description: Mexican Migration to the United States. Mexican migration from the 1850s to the present, emphasizing labor migrants to the United States.

HIST 386.description: American Legal History. An introduction to the study of law from a historical perspective; explores the interaction of law, culture and politics from the Revolution through the New Deal.

HIST 391.description: Feminist Histories of South Asia. History of South Asia with attention to questions of gender, sexuality and power with a focus on the eighteenth, nineteenth and twentieth centuries.

HIST 427.description: The German Question: Nation and Identity in Modern Central Europe. A seminar on the making, unmaking and re-making of the German  nation-state, with particular attention to issues of race, class  and gender in German identity.

HIST 456.description: Race, Slavery, and the Making of the Atlantic World. Introduction to the literature of the Atlantic World with a focus on slavery and its role in the emergence of the modern era. Seminar enrollment limited to 15 students.

HIST 460.description: War, Race, and the Constitution. Examines the World War II incarceration of Japanese Americans and its impact on issues of civil liberties as well as national security.

HIST 490.description: Directed Research.  Individual research and readings. Not available for graduate credit.

HIST 492.description: Honors Thesis. Writing of the honors thesis; for students in the History Honors Program.

HIST 493.description: Law, History and Culture Honors Thesis Seminar. Writing of the honors thesis; capstone for students in the Law, History and Culture major.

HIST 500.description: Introduction to Graduate Historical Studies.  Techniques, theories, and sub-disciplines of history.

HIST 514.description: Studies in Modern European History, 1789-1914. Readings and current bibliography in the history of Europe from  the French Revolution to the outbreak of World War I; emphasis on  cultural history approaches.

HIST 566.description: Historical Scholarship on North America to 1800. Introduction to research in the fields of American Indian,  colonial America, Atlantic world, and the early United States.   Open only to graduate students.

HIST 567.description: Historical Scholarship on 19th Century America. Introduction to historiography and research in the political,  economic, social, cultural, and intellectual history of the 19th  Century United States.

HIST 590.description: Directed Research.  Research leading to the master's degree. Maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department. Graded CR/NC.

HIST 594A.description: Master's Thesis.  Credit on acceptance of thesis. Graded IP/CR/NC

HIST 594B.description: Master's Thesis.  Credit on acceptance of thesis. Graded IP/CR/NC

HIST 594Z.description: Master's Thesis. Credit on acceptance of Thesis. Graded CR/NC.

HIST 595.description: Practicum in Teaching the Liberal Arts. Basic principles of history pedagogy, with emphasis on practical applications and the importance of career-long skill development. Required for first semester teaching assistants in history. Graded CR/NC.

HIST 617.description: Seminar in Russian History.  Directed research in historical problems.

HIST 790.description: Research.  Research leading to the doctorate. Maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department. Graded CR/NC.

HIST 794A.description: Doctoral Dissertation. Credit on acceptance of Dissertation.

HIST 794B.description: Doctoral Dissertation. Credit on acceptance of Dissertation.

HIST 794C.description: Doctoral Dissertation. Credit on acceptance of Dissertation.

HIST 794D.description: Doctoral Dissertation. Credit on acceptance of Dissertation.

HIST 794Z.description: Doctoral Dissertation. Credit on acceptance of Dissertation.

HT 500.description: Global Hospitality and Tourism. History, theories, trends and impacts relevant to global hospitality and tourism.

HT 505.description: Managing Service Quality in Hospitality and Tourism. Strategic management of service quality in hospitality and tourism.

HT 510.description: Marketing Strategies for Hospitality and Tourism. Principles, strategies and techniques relevant to marketing in hospitality and tourism.

HT 515.description: Financial Management in Hospitality and Tourism. Financial analysis methods to support sound, evidence-based decision-making in hospitality and tourism organizations.

HT 530.description: Strategic Human Resources in Hospitality and Tourism. Broad range of human resource concepts and strategies relevant to hospitality and tourism organizations.

HT 535.description: Applied Research Methods for Hospitality and Tourism. Applied research methods relevant to evidence-based decision-making in hospitality and tourism.

HT 550.description: Hospitality and Tourism Events. Analysis, planning and evaluation of meetings and events in hospitality and tourism settings.

HT 555.description: Hospitality and Tourism Capstone. Students synthesize knowledge and skills gained throughout the program in a culminating capstone project.

HBIO 120.description: Introduction to Human and Evolutionary Biology. Introduction to the major and field of human and evolutionary biology; sub-disciplines, career options and areas for research; guest speakers.

HBIO 202.description: Nutrition for Life. To develop an understanding of Nutrition, especially as it         pertains to optimal health and prevention of diseases. A study of  macro and micro nutrients.

HBIO 205.description: The Science of Sport. The physiological and nutritional basis of human performance. Factors that facilitate and limit athletic achievement. Lecture, 3 hours; laboratory, 2 hours. Not available for major credit. Duplicates credit in former EXSC 205Lxg.

HBIO 210.description: Mediterranean and Healthy Lifestyles in the World. Explores and contrasts the core components of the traditional mediterranean lifestyle to those of other lifestyles in the world. Biological and anthropological perspectives for following sustainable lifestyles to improve and maintain personal health.

HBIO 250.description: The Pharmacology of Performance-Enhancing Drugs. Evaluation of drugs, nutritional supplements, and ergogenic aids that are purported to enhance human athletic performance.

HBIO 301.description: Human Anatomy . Major organ systems; functional implications of their relationships; gross and microscopic examination with an emphasis on practical skills in recognizing, dissecting, and differentiating anatomical structures. Duplicates credit in former EXSC 301L.

HBIO 302.description: Nutrition and Metabolism. Gastrointestinal physiology and energy metabolism as it relates to macronutrient intake. Theories and principles of nutrition and     their impact on metabolic regulation. Prerequisites: BISC 220L or  BISC 221L. Duplicates credit in former EXSC 200.

HBIO 309.description: The Human Machine. An exploration of how the human body works and why it works the way it does; draws from the fields of anatomy, biomechanics, physiology, engineering and paleoanthropology.

HBIO 324.description: Integrative Pathophysiology. Analysis of the immunological processes and pathophysiological changes that occur as consequences of various human diseases and conditions.

HBIO 360.description: Nutrition and Disease. Principles of diet therapy for the prevention and treatment of human disease.

HBIO 408.description: Biomechanics. Kinematic and kinetic analysis of human motion. Emphasis on performance enhancement and injury prevention.

HBIO 420.description: Applied Human Physiology. The physiology of the respiratory, cardiovascular, renal, musculoskeletal, digestive, endocrine and nervous systems in humans, with application to human health and pathology.

HBIO 441.description: Prevention of Athletic Injuries. Application of scientific principles to conditioning, protecting, and rehabilitating the athlete.

HBIO 491.description: Laboratory Experience in Kinesiology. Practical laboratory experience in basic and applied exercise physiology, biochemistry, and/or biomechanics. Emphasizing development of laboratory techniques. Prerequisites: HBIO 203, HBIO 301, HBIO 302, HBIO 320. Duplicates credit in former EXSC 491.

HRM 500.description: Human Resource Strategy. Explores the strategic role that human resources management plays in providing organizations with sustained competitive advantages by unlocking the productive potential of employees human and social capital.

HRM 505.description: Organizational Culture and Employee Outcomes. Prepares students to create, foster, and manage organizations in which people thrive and perform at their best in order to retain talent and reduce costs in a sustainable way.

HRM 510.description: Leadership in Human Resources. Focuses on developing the critical social intelligence skills needed to lead people and change through increased self-awareness, understanding of interpersonal differences, and greater influence.

HRM 515.description: Organization Design. Equips students with a deeper understanding of how to design and develop organizations to increase performance and effectiveness and includes sections on strategy, work, and management processes.

HRM 520.description: Talent Management. Examines talent management processes that impact employee experience and engagement and explores ways to improve data driven decision making processes including workforce and succession planning.

HRM 525.description: Total Rewards. Provides a comprehensive look at the employee rewards strategies that human resource practitioners promote and manage including compensation, performance management, benefits, and non-monetary rewards.

HRM 530.description: Learning and Development. Prepares students to identify, design, and implement effective learning and development interventions and strategies that drive results and enhance organizational competitiveness.

HRM 535.description: Employee Relations. Applies practical approaches to building positive employee and labor relations and solving related problems through increased employee motivation, effectiveness, and retention.

HRM 540.description: Human Resources Analytics. Examines and emphasizes strategies and techniques to enable improved organizational and human capital decisions by directing the organizational analytics for more actionable insights.

HRM 545.description: Management of Diverse and Global Human Resources. Analyzes today's global HR environment with consideration to individual well-being and community alignment, focusing on effective organizational strategies and best practices.

HRM 550.description: Change Management and Organization Development. Identifies the common challenges in organizational change management and explores the limitations and opportunities of different models of organizational change.

HRM 555.description: Anticipating the Future of Human Resources. Explores the forces and emerging trends that are reshaping work, the workforce and workplace  and how to address these transformational changes and be effective as a Human Resources leader.

ISE 105.description: Introduction to Industrial and Systems Engineering. A combination of plant tours, laboratory experiences, and lecture  are used to introduce the philosophy, subject matter, aims, goals,  and techniques of industrial and systems engineering.

ISE 220.description: Foundations of Probability Modeling. Techniques for modeling uncertainty: discrete and continuous random variables, probability distributions, expectations and conditional probability; Poisson processes, Markov chains and queuing decision models.

ISE 225.description: Foundations of Data Analysis. Sampling distributions; confidence intervals and hypothesis testing; analysis of variance; regression; data aggregation; prediction and classification.

ISE 315.description: Engineering Project Management. Managing a project intended to create an engineered system.  Methods, processes, tools.  Lessons-learned from actual practice.  Case studies from real projects.  Presentations by student teams.

ISE 330.description: Optimization. Modeling, solution analysis and applications of complex decision problems using linear, dynamic and integer optimization.

ISE 349.description: Enterprise Data Analytics. Methodology to store, organize, cleanse, harmonize and stage enterprise data for analytics. Report, visualize, slice and dice, forecast and predict trends.

ISE 350.description: Principles and Practices of Systems Engineering. Systems as complex collaborative ensembles of interconnected components. Theory and practice of requirements, design, implementation, testing, deployment, operation and disposal. Case studies from real projects.

ISE 370.description: Human Factors in Work and Systems Design. Role of humans in technological systems; human-systems integration; ergonomics; anthropometry and workstation design; work methods and measurement; human error, safety and accident analysis.

ISE 382.description: Database Systems: Storage and Retrieval using SQL. Data models for industry applications. Modeling and designing robust databases. Implementing and querying databases with SQL. Innovations in database applications.

ISE 410.description: Planning and Scheduling for Production and Supply Chains. Production, resource and service planning, forecasting, scheduling, vendor and location selection, inventory; integrated decision systems for the control of production, services and supply chains.

ISE 435.description: Discrete Systems Simulation. Modeling of complex discrete event systems, input and output analysis, system evaluation via experimentation on the simulation model, applications to industrial and systems engineering problems.

ISE 440.description: Socio-Technical Systems and Work Organizations. Design, modeling and analysis of complex systems, challenges they present and methods for resolving those challenges. Impact of technology on work and organizational design.

ISE 490.description: Directed Research.  Individual research and readings. Not available for graduate credit.

ISE 495A.description: Senior Design Project. Investigate client organization operations, evaluate alternative designs to meet client needs, complete preliminary design review.

ISE 495B.description: Senior Design Project. Develop the detailed design including countermeasures for risks, complete critical design review, implement the project plan, close-out the project.

ISE 508.description: Health Care Operations Improvement. Strategies to improve hospital operations, including supply chains, staffing, informatics, data analytics and patient flow.

ISE 514.description: Advanced Production Planning and Scheduling. Dependencies among long, intermediate and short-range planning and scheduling of production systems considering objectives, technological constraints and solution algorithms.

ISE 515.description: Engineering Project Management. Methods, processes and tools for managing projects to create engineered systems. Project management; engineering economics; risk management. Industry-drawn large-scale engineering case studies. Team project presentations.

ISE 519.description: Engineering Management of Systems Integration. Foundations of systems integration; advanced topics in systems integration including generative artificial intelligence (AI); data analytics for predicting and supporting engineering decisions.

ISE 521.description: Foundations of Analytics. Foundational tools, technologies and methodologies for analytics. The statistical basis of analytics. Understanding and preparing data. Python, SQL and exploratory data analysis.

ISE 530.description: Optimization Methods for Analytics. Fundamentals of Linear Programming, Integer Programming, quadratic and nonlinear programming for analytics and data science problems.

ISE 537.description: Financial Analytics. Modern portfolio theory and optimal decision-making problems in finance. Market microstructure and high-frequency trading. Machine learning models for quantitative finance.

ISE 538.description: Markov Models for Performance Analysis. Stochastic processes: conditional expectation, Poisson process, discrete time Markov chains, continuous time Markov chains with queueing applications, non-Markovian queues and reliability.

ISE 541.description: Time Series and Spatial Data Analysis. Theory and application of time series and spatial data analytics; Box-Jenkins statistical methods (ARIMA), time series modeling and forecasting; modern spatial statistical methods.

ISE 543.description: Enterprise Cloud Analytics. Project-based course covers developing scalable analytics solutions using major cloud platforms, focusing on data management, machine learning and enterprise applications.

ISE 544.description: Leading and Managing Engineering Teams. Design and management of engineering teams. Group decision-making, motivation, leadership, infrastructure requirements, performance measurement, team diversity, conflict and integration.

ISE 545.description: Principles and Practices of Global Innovation. The content, context and practice of technology innovation in competitive global markets focusing on how social and cultural contexts shape customer needs and market demands.

ISE 558.description: Fundamentals of Data Engineering. Essentials of data engineering, focusing on data architecture, data warehousing, ETL processes, big data technologies, and data quality.

ISE 561.description: Economic Analysis of Engineering Projects. Economic evaluations of engineering systems for both government and private industry; quantitative techniques for evaluating non-monetary consequences; formal treatment of risk and uncertainty.

ISE 562.description: Decision Analysis. Decisions under uncertainty; utility theory; multiattribute utility; probability elicitation; conjugate distributions; decision analysis applications, framing, modeling using spreadsheets or software; cognitive biases, behavioral decision theory.

ISE 580.description: Performance Analysis with Simulation. Introduction to modeling and analysis of stochastic systems, with an emphasis on discrete-event simulation of non-Markovian systems.

ISE 588.description: Management of Rapid Product Development. Rapid Product Development (RPD) including: agile frameworks for RPD; minimum viable products; rapid prototyping; continuous improvement techniques; user feedback integration; data-driven decision-making.

ISE 590.description: Directed Research.  Research leading to the master's degree; maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department. Graded CR/NC.

ISE 599.description: Special Topics.  Course content will be selected each semester to reflect current trends and developments in the field of industrial and systems engineering.

ISE 620.description: Foundations of Stochastic Processes. Stochastic processes, conditional expectation, Poisson processes, renewal processes, regenerative processes, and discrete and continuous time Markov chains.

ISE 631.description: Linear Programming. Understanding optimization problems with constraints and extensions to the treatment of problems involving nonlinearity, uncertainty, discrete variables, logical constraints, multi-agent non-cooperative games and hierarchical problems.

ISE 651.description: Seminar in Industrial and Systems Engineering. Current research, guest speakers in the field; review papers; guidance in preparing research proposals and special projects.

ISE 790.description: Research. Research leading to the doctorate. Maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department. Graded CR/NC.

ISE 794B.description: Doctoral Dissertation. Credit on acceptance of Dissertation.

ISE 794D.description: Doctoral Dissertation. Credit on acceptance of Dissertation.

IDSN 515.description: Professional Practices Residential. One-week off-campus residential. Applied, intensive workshop format focused on solutions for real-world problems with input from industry experts.

IDSN 518.description: Innovation Practicum. Experiential learning through practical training.

IDSN 519.description: Professional Internship. Hands-on internship experience applying integrated design, business and technology skills to real organizational challenges, expanding students' capacity for innovation, strategic thinking, collaboration and career advancement.

IDSN 523.description: Product Design for User Experience. Fundamental methods, concepts and techniques necessary to design useful, functional and delightful digital products--including hands-on application of user research, Figma and team leadership.

IDSN 524.description: Physical Product Design. Initial design and development of consumer products; from ideation through visualization, market research, and prototyping to ready-to-market solutions; 3D modeling and 3D printing.

IDSN 529.description: Marketing Strategy for Startups. A focus on ideal marketing strategies for early-stage startups seeking to build communities of early adopters and beta testers for products, services, and systems.

IDSN 538.description: Extended Reality Technologies. Provides context for creating augmented and virtual reality by examining the technologies that enable them and the perspectives for new applications in virtual and physical spaces.

IDSN 540.description: Processes and Perspectives. Discipline-specific, cross-disciplinary and shared approaches to products, services, projects, systems, organizational development. Topics include creative and user-focused perspectives, feasibility analytics, lean startup techniques.

IDSN 542.description: Introduction to Machine Intelligence. Concepts and applications of artificial intelligence and machine learning; topics include agents, knowledge representation, classification systems, training models, decision trees, decision trees and ensemble learning

IDSN 547.description: Industry and Impact Projects. Practicum through which student teams serve as design strategists for industry collaborators, and learn advanced methods and processes to solve problems in collaborative, field-specific environments.

IDSN 577.description: Finance for Entrepreneurs. The life cycle of a new venture from idea to construction of an    enterprise to a decision about financial viability. Recommended  preparation: IDSN 525 Business Essentials.

IDSN 590.description: Directed Research. Research leading to the master's degree. Maximum units, which may be applied to the degree, to be determined by the department. Graded CR/NC.

IDSN 599.description: Special Topics. Selected topics in design, business and technology.

IAS 501A.description: Human Gross Anatomy. A complete dissection of the adult human body. Supplementary lectures and demonstrations. Emphasis on correlating development, structure and function. This course duplicates credit in former CNB 501a.

IAS 501B.description: Human Gross Anatomy. A complete dissection of the adult human body. Supplementary lectures and demonstrations. Emphasis on correlating development, structure and function. This course duplicates credit in former CNB 501b.

IAS 511A.description: Microscopic Anatomy I. Study of microscopic anatomy emphasizing embryonic origin of the body plan, cells, tissues, and organs; ultrastructural and functional correlations. Duplicates credit in former CNB 511a.

IAS 521.description: Neuroanatomy. Structure and function of the human nervous system with emphasis on central conduction pathways, especially those of clinical significance.

IAS 580.description: Teaching in the Anatomical Sciences. Introduces pedagogical principles of learning and assessment, effective content delivery and instructional design for anatomical teaching.

IAS 590.description: Directed Research. Research leading to the master's degree. Maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department.

IAS 790.description: Research. Research leading to the doctorate. Maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department.

IAS 794B.description: Doctoral Dissertation. Credit on acceptance of dissertation.

CTIN 101.description: Fundamentals of Procedural Media. Introduction to the procedural nature of interactive media and games, though the coding language Processing. Students will develop proficiency in reading and creating computational media.

CTIN 190.description: Introduction to Interactive Entertainment. Critical vocabulary and historical perspectives on interactive entertainment; students articulate their own ideas, while wrestling with the larger conceptual issues at play within the field.

lectures.instructor: TreaAndrea Russworm; Maynard Hearns; Ian Larson

CTIN 191.description: Survey of Themed Entertainment. Introduction to the field of themed entertainment and education design, covering its history, and, especially, current practice.

CTIN 290.description: Digital Media Workshop. Exploration of a variety of moving image aesthetics and methodologies in order to highlight how the language of cinema shapes contemporary digital and interactive media practices.

CTIN 291.description: Crew for Advanced Game Project. Hands-on creating experiences for students who want to work as crew on an advanced game project.

lectures.instructor: David White; Kathleen Bucklin; Mason Lieberman; Timothy Lee

CTIN 389.description: Game Development Principles. Concepts and projects relating to the implementation and presentation of digital games; core level design preproduction techniques.

CTIN 395.description: Miniature Golf Design. Workshop on the design of miniature golf holes, considering theming, experience and build.

other.instructor: Amanda Rosenberg; Waylon Dobson; Alexander Lieu

CTIN 401.description: Interface Design for Games. Introduction to the aesthetics, terminology and common trends of interface design for games. Topics include 2-D and 3-D spaces and user/camera perspectives.

CTIN 409.description: Producing Interactive Projects. An in-depth exploration of the development and production concepts woven into the USC Games curriculum and utilized in the professional games industry.

CTIN 410.description: Narrative Design Workshop. An exploration of characters and story worlds as they relate to gaming with an emphasis on emotionally rich environments in interactive entertainment.

CTIN 411.description: Tabletop Game Mechanics Seminar. Seminar on the design patterns and mechanics of successful tabletop games. Includes guest speakers on the latest trends in gaming content, tools, business and culture.

CTIN 412.description: Interactive Systems Design. An overview of systems thinking, complex systems, game economies and emergence with practical applications towards designing and balancing systems for games and interactivity.

CTIN 422.description: Games as Live Service Operations (GLO). Design and manage live-service games like Fortnite. Create games with functioning economies and community engagement. Support publicly available titles with new content and community events.

other.instructor: Jim Huntley; Kyle Ackerman; Hong Ly

CTIN 424.description: Streaming Production for Games. Learn how to produce and manage esports and livestreaming engagements with specific emphasis on planning and practical implementation.

CTIN 442.description: Dystopias: Games, Comics, Media. Examines video games, comics and media as we ask questions about the persistence of dystopian narratives in print and visual culture.

CTIN 444.description: Audio Expression. Foundational aesthetic principles and creative technologies for game audio. Processing, mixing, and controlling sound for games for expressive effect.

CTIN 452.description: Themed Entertainment Design. The fundamentals of design, technology, operations and process for the creation of themed entertainment experiences and story-centric place-making.

CTIN 455.description: Designing with Specialists for Themed Entertainment. Learn how to work with an industry speciality, and understand their contribution towards Themed Entertainment projects.

CTIN 457.description: Themed Entertainment Business Operations. The business of themed entertainment, focused on teaching literacy to communicate with business partners and understanding the basic needs of a themed entertainment project.

CTIN 458.description: Business and Management of Games. Overview of current business models in games and interactive media, methods for pitching and getting products funded; copyright and intellectual property.

CTIN 463.description: Anatomy of a Game. Examine two game products from concept to delivery; introduce students to each of the professional disciplines involved in making digital games. Recommended preparation: CTIN 488.

CTIN 468.description: Advanced Games Business. An advanced dive into the structure of the games industry with a focus on emerging trends and the future of games as business and entertainment.

CTIN 470.description: Unreal Game Engine Fundamentals. Introduction into the Unreal Game Engine which is used for Video Game Design as well as Virtual Production.

CTIN 488.description: Game Design Workshop. An introduction to making games. Students will explore the principles of game design through the entirely analog creation of card, board and tabletop games.

CTIN 489.description: Intermediate Game Design and Production. A follow-up to the introductory game design class, this course will introduce more advanced concepts in game design and game theories, including ideation, digital prototyping and level design.

CTIN 490.description: Directed Research. Individual research and readings. Not available for graduate credit.

CTIN 491.description: Advanced Game Project I. Students work in teams on pre-production and production of a functional digital game suitable for showcases, festivals, and further development.

CTIN 498.description: Game Art Capstone. Students work individually to create a Game Art project based on their interests, skills, abilities, and concentration.

CTIN 506.description: Procedural Expression. Developing procedural literacy in the analysis and creation of computational media; an introduction to how we create meaningful experiences using rules and interaction. Duplicates credit in former CTIN 400.

CTIN 529A.description: Graduate Advanced Game Project. Capstone course for assigned Game Directors or Area Leads to start an innovative, large-scale game project.

CTIN 532.description: Interactive Design and Production I. The development of interactive experiences with an emphasis on prototyping and development.

CTIN 534.description: Experiments in Interactivity I. Experimental studio course to explore concepts of structure, aesthetics and content of interactive experience design.

CTIN 541.description: Design for Interactive Media. Practical exploration and practicum on the fundamental process and principles of interactive media design. Students develop design and prototyping skills while working in collaborative teams.

CTIN 575.description: Health and Interactive Entertainment Research Lab. Emerging transdisciplinary research methods for conducting formative or summative evaluation of interactive entertainment-based interventions.

CTIN 582.description: Ideation and Concept Development. Learn the phases of ideation and preproduction while building multiple interactive prototypes.

CTIN 583.description: Game Development for Designers. The fundamentals of 3-D real time game engines, scripting for interactivity, and building games with digital tools.

CTIN 591.description: Crew for Graduate Advanced Game Project. Students from many disciplines work in large teams to create an innovative, large-scale interactive media or game project.

INTD 500.description: Ethics and Accountability in Biomedical Research. The purpose of this course is to engage current (and potential)  research trainees in discussions about the responsible conduct of  science.  The course is designed as an option for meeting current  federal regulations which require that all predoctoral and  postdoctoral fellows paid from federal contracts and grants have a  component of ethical training.  Graded CR/NC.

INTD 502.description: Foundations in Biomedical Sciences - I. Provides foundational knowledge in several key areas of biology: gene regulation and epigenetics, protein chemistry and physiology, and practice in critical review of literature.

INTD 550.description: Introduction to Pathology. Normal histology and introduction to basic pathological concepts. Provides a solid and basic understanding of normal structures and how they relate to function.

lectures.instructor: Louis Dubeau; Leslie Khawli; Evelyn Valdovinos

INTD 574.description: Medical Biology Seminar. Selected topics in systems biology and disease.

INTD 577.description: Writing in the Biomedical and Biological Sciences. Writing instruction for graduate students focusing on grant proposals and scientific papers. Includes both writing and providing critiques of classmates work. Lectures and discussion. Open only to doctoral students in the school of Medicine.

INTD 596.description: Internship for Curricular Practical Training. Part-time or full-time, practical work experience in the student's field of study. The internship must be located at an off-campus facility. Students are individually supervised by faculty. May not be taken until the student has completed at least one semester of enrollment in the graduate program.

INTD 600.description: Student Research Presentation. Students prepare and present their own research to an audience of faculty and peers. Graded CR/NC. Open only to graduate students.

INTD 620.description: Medical Students Elective Program. Opportunities for Medical students as preceptors, in research  laboratories or in field medical services under guidance of  sponsors approved by faculty committees. Graded CR/NC.

INTD 622.description: Pre-clinical System Block for Health, Technology and Engineering                                 .
